title: Xanthan gum, 21 CFR 172.695: food additives permitted for direct addition to food for human consumption
journal: Code of Federal Regulations, title 21, section 172.695, read in the electronic Code of Federal Regulations, edition of 1 October 2026
funder: US Food and Drug Administration; the text is federal regulation codified by the Office of the Federal Register.
result: The food additive xanthan gum may be safely used in food under prescribed conditions: it is a polysaccharide gum derived from Xanthomonas campestris by a pure-culture fermentation process and purified by recovery with isopropyl alcohol, containing D-glucose, D-mannose and D-glucuronic acid as the dominant hexose units and manufactured as the sodium, potassium or calcium salt; the strain must be non-pathogenic and non-toxic in man or other animals and the process must render the additive free of viable cells. Specifications: residual isopropyl alcohol not above 750 parts per million, a minimum viscosity of 600 centipoises for a 1% solution with 1% potassium chloride at 75 °F, a positive locust bean gum gel test and more than 1.5% pyruvic acid by weight. The additive is used in accordance with good manufacturing practice as a stabiliser, emulsifier, thickener, suspending agent, bodying agent or foam enhancer in foods for which standards of identity do not preclude such use; no numerical limit on use is set. The container label must bear the name of the additive, the designation 'food grade' and adequate directions for use.
